title: Watch a motion loop at the sizes it will really be used at
goal: A swing that reads beautifully on a big canvas is a shimmer at the size an icon is actually used, and a tenth of a second lag is six frames that nobody can see at full speed. So the way you judge a motion is to watch it loop side by side at the real sizes, with a speed you can slow right down.
notes:
Slice 4 of 5 from the answered study. This is what replaces scrubbing a playhead: the review for something that loops is watching it loop.

MOCK: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-phase-wt.html step 6 (0.25x, lag included) and icon-animate-wt steps 7 and 8.

There is already an IconPreviewsStrip in the app showing an icon at several sizes; this is that strip learning to play. Check whether it is Next only before touching it, and keep current-release behaviour unchanged.

PERF: the preview redraws continuously, so it touches the composite path. Measure and put a perf note in the commit per the repo rules.
acceptance: The preview strip plays the motion, looping, at 16, 24, 32 and 48 points at once
A speed control slows it to a quarter, and everything including the lag between parts slows with it
Play and pause is one control and also the space bar
The preview keeps up while a motion is being edited, without stuttering the rest of the app

log.note: deps set: the motion model lands first, then this
